title: What If You Climbed Olympus Mons, the Tallest Volcano?

scenes.text: What if you climbed Olympus Mons? The hardest part isn't the steepness.
It rises about 21 kilometers above Mars's average level, roughly two and a half times Everest.
The slope averages just 5 percent, but the volcano is about 600 kilometers wide.
At the top, you'd stand beside a caldera more than 60 kilometers wide, six collapsed craters stacked together.
Mars's low gravity let lava pile up higher, and with no moving plates, one hot spot kept building in place.
It may have erupted as recently as 25 million years ago. Your hike would end on a volcano that might still be active.
